nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $m$, the rook domination polynomial of the $n \times m$ board is the integer polynomial $D_{n,m}(x) = \sum_{k=0}^{nm} d_{n,m}(k)\, x^k$, where $d_{n,m}(k)$ is the number of $k$-element sets of cells of the $n \times m$ board that are dominating sets of the rook graph on that board.
nodes.title: Domination polynomial of the rook graph

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $m$, a finite set $S$ of cells of the $n \times m$ board dominates the rook graph on that board if and only if for every cell $(i, j)$, some cell of $S$ lies in row $i$ or some cell of $S$ lies in column $j$.
nodes.title: Dominating sets of the rook graph

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $m$, the rook graph on the $n \times m$ board is the simple graph whose vertices are the cells $(i, j)$ with $0 \le i < n$ and $0 \le j < m$, in which two cells are adjacent if and only if they are distinct and lie in the same row (same $i$) or the same column (same $j$).
